p.t: In short
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: Your return rules must match each supplier's return rules, because the supplier decides what you can offer.

Every return window needs an end date, such as 30 days, and it must be written on your site.
Put shipping and return details where buyers see them before they pay.
Products from suppliers that take no returns must be marked "not eligible for returns" on every page.
Before you publish, check your Contact Us page and policy pages with **Google Gemini** (Google's AI tool) and fix what it flags.
Your return policy must say **where to send items**, and that the return address comes only after your return is approved.
Never publish AI text that still has **empty square brackets** or example values you did not check. Match every value to how your store really works.
For a new store, keep the **default settings**. Change them later, when you know each supplier's real rules.
Before you start: supplier terms and policy basis
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: A **supplier** is the company that holds the product and ships it to your buyer.
Dropshipping means you sell this way and never keep the stock yourself.
Base your store's **return policy** (the rules for sending items back and getting money back) on each supplier's return policy.

If a supplier allows **30-day** free returns, your store can offer the same.
If a supplier allows **no returns**, mark those products on the site as not eligible for returns.
Read the **signed supplier approval documents**, the papers where the supplier agrees to work with you.
These papers state each supplier's return terms. Your store's return policy is set around them.
Match your **return window** (the number of days a buyer has to ask for a return) to what the supplier allows.

Read the supplier's agreement documents **before** you set the policy.
Show any **longer supplier window** on the product pages.
Return responsibility for heavy items depends on each supplier's policy. You learn it when the supplier approves you.

If suppliers charge **return shipping** (the cost of sending the item back) or **restocking fees** (a fee kept from the refund to cover handling the returned item), state those fees in your shipping and returns policy.

Base that policy on the supplier's terms.
Return policies differ between brands.

Your store's returns policy should summarise **all** supplier policies.
Each supplier's policy should be noted in the retailer paperwork.
Before you list a brand, check its **return process** (how returns are handled from start to finish).
Brands with supplier-level support and clear policies reduce return and **warranty** problems. A warranty is the maker's promise to repair or replace faulty goods.

Expect **higher return rates** in some niches (narrow product markets).
Avoid those niches when you choose products.
Compare your return policy with the **top two or three competitors** (other stores selling the same kind of product) in your niche.
A policy with refunds within **30 days** without a reason, a restocking fee of **15% to 20%**, and customer-paid return shipping is acceptable if competitors do the same.

You can set the fee lower to stand out.
To set return shipping fees, look at the return policies of your top future competitors.
Model yours on them.
Choose whether to charge the **actual cost** or a **fixed amount** for return shipping.
Shipping policy content
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: The shipping policy must be clear enough for a reviewer to understand within **one minute**.
It must state when orders ship after purchase. "Ship" here means "send out", also called **dispatch**. A range of days is acceptable.

It must state the **average transit time** (how many days the parcel takes to arrive).
It must state the shipping cost, including whether shipping is **free**.
Vague shipping policies are a known cause of **compliance problems** (breaking ad or platform rules, which can get a store blocked).

Avoid any wording that could be read as misleading.
Use this template for the shipping policy text:
Once your purchase goes through, you'll get an order confirmation email. We dispatch every order within [X] days of placement and send you an email with the tracking number as soon as it leaves us.
Across the United States, every order ships free through [carrier(s) you typically use]. Choose free shipping and transit takes [X] to [Y] business days.
If the store offers faster options, add this line: customers who need quicker delivery can pick [upgraded delivery option] at checkout, and those expedited rates are calculated live at checkout.
If the store ships internationally at no charge, add this line: every international order ships free, and with free international shipping transit runs [X] to [Y] weeks.

Reference figures from the US example in the sample text: dispatch within **3 days**.
US transit is **3 to 5 business days**. A business day is a working day, Monday to Friday.

International transit is **1 to 3 weeks**.
The carrier is **USPS** (US Postal Service, a US delivery company).
If you do not yet know your real average shipping times, check competitors' shipping pages to estimate them.
The policy can be updated later. It only needs to exist and be accurate **from the start**.
Shipping policy content (continued)
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: A **high-ticket** dropshipping store (one that sells expensive products) usually **does not ship internationally**.

Publish the international shipping paragraph only if the store actually ships abroad.
A store that ships worldwide should state the international transit time **in weeks**.
The shipping page should list the expected shipping time for **each supplier or brand**, because suppliers ship at different speeds.
Update these times as they become clear, for example after a few weeks of order data.
Shipping time must be stated in the store's policies, along with contact methods, the return policy and product descriptions.

Missing details are a common reason for a **store review** (a check by an ad platform or payment provider). (2023)
Keep store policies **short and clear**, not long legal texts.

Sample policies are only a few sentences each.
Many shoppers do not know a new store.

Write the shipping policy (cost, delivery time, carrier) and the returns policy in **plain English**.
Make them **better than competitors'** policies.
The contact page must offer at least **two** ways to reach the business, such as a phone number and a business email.
A contact form may be added, but it does not replace the two methods.
Until dedicated support mailboxes exist, use **support@ followed by your domain** (for example support@yourdomain.com) in the policy templates.
Replace it with the real mailbox once it exists.
Shipping and returns page placement
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: Shoppers read the shipping policy **before** they spend a lot of money.
Place shipping information where buyers look before ordering, and make it easy to find and complete.
The returns and exchange page answers what happens if the buyer is unhappy. Buyers ask this **before** purchasing.

Keep it visible **before checkout** (the payment step) to reduce hesitation.
The shipping page can link to the returns policy.
A short shipping statement with a link to the returns page reduces questions.

Leaving the return policy off the page leaves shoppers worried about damaged or unwanted items.
State **easy returns** clearly on the page.

Most merchandise sold by mail ships subject to return.
Return rights are a standard part of **direct response selling** (selling through ads that push buyers to act now).

A clear return policy removes the buyer's risk.
Do **not** open the returns and exchanges policy by default, especially a harsh one.

Place it in an **expandable section** (a box that opens when clicked) for curious buyers.
A long multi-step return process can scare off undecided visitors.
Pre-footer trust column (the strip just above the bottom of the page): use a clear header such as "Easy returns".
Link that header to the returns policy page **once that page exists**. Until then, leave the link empty.
Policy pages such as shipping or terms are needed **before** they are linked in the pre-footer.

In the example, a temporary link to terms of service was used. Replace it with the correct page later.
Publish the shipping policy and the returns policy on the store.
Make sure everyone handling orders has read **both** before working on them.
Free shipping, add-ons and accessories
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: A **free standard shipping** offer on all products is a common store policy.
**Expedited shipping** (faster shipping for extra money) or **white glove delivery** (staff carry the item in and set it up) can be offered as **paid add-ons**.
Conditional free shipping (free only when set conditions are met) is set up on the shipping page of **Shopify** (the online store software).

Create **separate shipping profiles** (saved sets of shipping rules) for each case.
Each profile lists the criteria that must be met for it to apply.

Accessories with **flat-rate shipping** (one fixed shipping price) should be sold **only as add-ons** to a main product.
Do not list accessories as standalone products.
Do not include accessories in ads and **product feeds** (product lists sent to ad platforms).
When offering free shipping, a customer return means the shipping cost already paid may **not be recovered**.

Design the return policy around **each supplier's** return rules, not a single store-wide policy.
Advertising free shipping while charging customers for return shipping is acceptable.

The return costs must be **clearly disclosed** in the policy.
Clarity in advance prevents complaints about shipping.

Return windows should **always have an end date**.
Unlimited free returns make it impossible to tell when a product is profitable.

Match the store's return window to the supplier's policy.
Example: **30 days** when the supplier allows 30 days.

The US average return window for physical products is about **30 days**.
Supplier windows can be **14, 30, 60 or up to 180 days**. (2023)

No general US legal return period exists for ordinary products that the store must offer. (2023)
This is general information, not legal advice. (2023)

A UK retailer may be required to offer a **14-day** return policy for consumer goods.
Check local rules before setting the policy.
The US has no equivalent blanket rule for most products.

p.t:
Each row applies to the case stated.
**30 days**

Applies to: Standard window for a new dropship store, because it usually follows supplier return policies. Adjust later once supplier policies are known.
**30 days**

Applies to: Store-wide default when suppliers share similar terms; exceptions only for extreme outliers (2023).
**30 days from delivery**

Applies to: Source B general window for most items in new condition.
**30 days from delivery**

Applies to: Australian caravan parts retailer, change-of-mind returns in original condition.
**30 days from purchase date**

Applies to: Source D sample policy template, where the window counts from the purchase date.
**30 days, with a 14-day window for one supplier**
Applies to: General store policy at 30 days; a supplier with a 14-day window gets the 14-day window stated on its product pages and is listed as an exclusion. (2023)

**7 days**
Applies to: Furniture brand, Source B.
**14 days**

Applies to: Mirror brand, Source B; no returns once installed.
**3 days from delivery**
Applies to: Shopify default example in the sample text, with an option to extend for weekends or holidays. This conflicts with the 14-day text in the sample template and must be aligned. (2026)

**14, 30, 90, Unlimited or Custom days**
Applies to: Options in the Shopify return rules settings.
Return windows differ by brand.
A general **30-day** window applies to most items in new condition. A brand can have its own window.
For a 30-day window, the Source D template reads "You have [number of days] days from the purchase date to initiate a return."

Choose the start point, **purchase date or delivery**, and state it in the policy.
Match the store's return window to the supplier.
When suppliers differ, use the window in the store's general policy and show the exception on product pages.
Customer can return within 30 days on the store-wide default, with a **10% restocking fee** and customer pays return shipping (example brand structure).
Return conditions and eligibility
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t:
Returned items must go back in **original packaging** with all parts.
A returned item must be **unused**.

It must be kept in the state it arrived in.
It must still be in its original packaging.
Any return needs a **receipt** or other proof of purchase.
A **change-of-mind return** (the buyer changed their mind, the item is not faulty) can be accepted even when special packaging has been opened.

This is true as long as the product itself is in **original condition**.
Record this condition, because it decides whether a return is accepted.
For change-of-mind returns, the store's policy should copy the supplier's policy for **gently used** products. (2023)
The store cannot send the item back to the supplier under different terms. (2023)
Return conditions to state in the policy: [L0539 student input] "New, unused, in original packaging, all accessories included" is the example condition set.
Return wording for a dropshipping store reads: "Items must be returned in their original condition."
Record the return conditions as **one clear rule set per supplier** when they differ.
Typical exceptions to change-of-mind returns include the following.

**Sanitation products** (toilets, bidets and similar bathroom items) that were opened or installed.
**Electronics**, unless in sealed original packaging.

Items **sold by the metre**.
**Specially ordered** items.
Installed, modified or used items.
**Free freight** included in the price can be deducted from the refund.
**Bidets and toilets** (personal hygiene products) cannot be returned once they are **opened or installed**.

**Food and flowers** (perishables, things that spoil fast), **gift cards**, and **health and personal-care products** cannot be sent back.
This is the exclusion in the Source D sample policy.

If a product is an **ingestible** (anything you eat or swallow), a **hygiene item**, a **pre-owned** good (used before), or a **final-sale** item (cannot be returned or exchanged), the return policy must say so.
Non-returnable items and excluded products (continued)
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t:
These categories are often excluded from standard refunds.
The exclusion must appear on the policy page. Do not leave it for the buyer to discover.

Refunds apply only to **full-price items**.
Discounted goods are not refundable in the sample policy.
A supplier with a no-return policy should be matched on your store.
Add a note to each product page from that supplier. The note says the item is **not eligible for returns** unless it arrives **defective** (faulty) or **damaged** (broken).

Use the supplier's **exact wording**. (2023)
Products the supplier does not take back must be marked as **non-returnable** on the policy page.

Mark them also on **each product page**. This prevents disputes when a customer later asks for a return.
Suppliers without a return policy can still be sold.

The product pages and the return policy page must state that those products are **not eligible for return**.
If a supplier refuses returns for a product, you have two options.
**Option 1:** mark the product as not eligible for returns on its page.
**Option 2:** ship the product to a **fulfilment centre** (a warehouse that packs and ships orders) that you control, if you want to sell it.

If a supplier refuses returns for **damaged items**, do not accept returns for those products either.
State this exclusion in the return policy.

Also state it on that supplier's product pages. (2025)
When some suppliers accept no returns, state that **clearly** on their product pages, where customers see it before buying.
Products from suppliers that do not accept returns should be **excluded** from the return policy.
Add a note on those product pages and in the **shipping and returns tab** (the section of the product page) that the items are not eligible for returns.
Products from suppliers that accept no returns must be named as not eligible for return on the **shipping and returns page**.
Name them also on their **product pages**.
Wording for a no-return product: "This item is not eligible for returns unless it arrives defective or damaged. [Use the supplier's exact return wording]"
Exclusion wording template
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: This item is not eligible for returns unless it arrives defective or damaged. [Use the supplier's exact return wording]
Exclusion: products from [Supplier name] are eligible for return only if they arrive defective or damaged.
Procedure for adding a no-return policy for a supplier that does not accept returns:
1. **Update** the shipping and returns policy page with a note listing the affected supplier or products.

2. **Add** the same note to every product page from that supplier, in the shipping and returns tab.
3. **Use** wording such as "This product is not eligible for returns; all sales are final."

Procedure for a non-returnable brand (2025):
1. **Keep** your general return policy for all brands.
2. **Add** an exception at the bottom of the policy. It states that products from the non-returnable brand are not eligible for return.
3. **Replace** the standard return text on each product page of that brand with a statement that the product is not eligible for return.

Follow the procedure in when a brand has no returns.
**Do not** use a general no-return rule for a supplier whose terms are otherwise general.
Put the exclusion **only on that supplier's pages**.
Restocking fees and return shipping costs depend on each supplier's return policy.

Customers usually pay return shipping, but this varies by supplier.
A restocking fee should **match the supplier's fee**, not be added on top of it.

The purpose is to **avoid losing money** on returns, not to make profit from them. (2025)
Restocking fees and return terms can differ per brand. (2025)

Show them on the general return policy page. (2025)
Optionally, show them in expandable sections on each product page. (2025)
Use this structure for a brand-specific return policy (2025):
Our return policies vary by brand. Please see the list below for the return policy of each brand. Brand A products can be returned within 30 days.

A 10% restocking fee applies, and you are responsible for return shipping costs. Brand B products can be returned within 60 days. A 20% restocking fee applies, and you are responsible for return shipping costs.
Replace the brand names, return windows and fees with the exact terms from each supplier.
Restocking fee values by source
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t:
Each row applies to the case stated.
**10% to 15% of order price**

Applies to: Charged only if the top 2 to 3 competitors charge it; otherwise omit to remain competitive (2024).
**15% to 20%**

Applies to: Acceptable if competitors do the same (2024).
**15%**
Applies to: Large items.

**15%**
Applies to: Steam shower or bathtub that fails local inspection, unit still in original packaging.
**25%**

Applies to: Same steam shower or bathtub when it was opened, or opened and assembled.
**10% (normally)**
Applies to: Australian caravan parts retailer, refund on request.

**10% or 20%**
Applies to: Brand structure examples (Brand A and Brand B).
**5% or 10%**

Applies to: Lower fee used to beat a competitor's 15% (2023).
**None**
Applies to: Source D Shopify default; Source D sample policy; new dropship store default.
Restocking fees can also apply to **damaged packaging**, to **inspection and testing** of appliances, and to items with **multiple components**.

Expect fees beyond the standard percentage in these cases.
If a store charges **no restocking fee**, state this clearly.

Make it prominent in the refund policy.
**Google** (the search and ads platform) views a zero-dollar restocking fee favourably.

If a customer asks for a return fee receipt, a restocking fee can be charged and documented in the return policy. (2023)
This lets customers see the fee **before buying**. (2023)
For a **non-defective** return, the customer normally pays the return shipping fee.

Damaged or defective items are replaced at **no cost** to the customer.
Returns should stay a **very small share** of total sales. (2021)

Return shipping costs are **always** charged to the customer. (2024)
Customers usually pay return shipping.

For a damaged item, the customer does **not** pay for the return.
Free returns are the default for stores of this kind. (2023)

Customers pay for return shipping on almost all stores. (2023)
Restocking fees are the alternative. (2023)
Return shipping and who pays (continued)
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t:
If a supplier offers **free return shipping**, absorb the cost and do not charge the customer. (2023)
Otherwise, the customer pays. (2023)

For damaged or defective returns, the **supplier** should pay the return shipping. (2023)
Supplier applications may ask who pays. The answer is the supplier. (2023)
If a **store-caused problem** (wrong or defective item) occurs, the store can cover all return shipping and refund the original shipping cost.

Keep the store-caused case separate from **buyer's remorse** (the buyer simply changing their mind).
The store covers all shipping for defective or wrong items.
**Heavy products:** the refund policy must state that a customer who requests a refund pays the shipping cost to send the item out and the return shipping.

This applies **even if** the original order had free shipping.
For heavy products, this can be about **35 dollars each way**.

State this on the shipping page, in the order confirmation and in the terms.
Shipping cost for the return: "Customer is responsible" for buyer's remorse.

"Store covers all shipping" for defective or wrong items (example input).
For a buyer's remorse return, the customer can be made responsible for return shipping.
The restocking fee terms must be stated.
For **warranty claims** (requests for repair or replacement under the maker's warranty), the customer returned the faulty item to the seller at their own cost.
The seller paid to send the repaired or replacement item back once a **manufacturing fault** (a flaw from how the item was made) was confirmed.
If no manufacturing fault was found, the customer paid the freight for the item's return.
Free return postage in the Source B example was limited to **3 months** for spare parts and **12 months** for other items.

If no manufacturing fault was found, the customer paid the freight back.
Source D sample: the customer pays return postage.
That postage is **not reimbursed**.
Shopify return rules: return shipping cost is set to "Customer provides return shipping" or "Flat rate return shipping" (one fixed price).
Shopify default: the **customer pays** for return shipping.
Prepaid return labels
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: If prepaid return labels are used, the policy should state whether the label cost is deducted from the refund.

Example input: "Yes, cost deducted from refund."
Exchanges use prepaid shipping labels in the default settings for a new dropship store.
The refund timeframe should be a fixed number of business days counted from when the item is received and inspected, for example within 7 business days.
Stating the start point of the clock prevents customers from expecting refunds on the day the return is shipped.
Sample refund rule: approved refunds go back to the original payment method within 5 to 7 business days after the returned item is inspected.
Partial refunds may apply to items not in original condition, damaged items, or returns after the window.
Refund wording from the lesson: "If you're unhappy with your products for any reason, we refund the full amount minus shipping.
To ask for a refund, email [business email] or phone [phone number]. [Add restocking fee, if any.] [Add brands or products that cannot be returned, if any.]"
If you're unhappy with your products for any reason, we refund the full amount minus shipping.
To ask for a refund, email [business email] or phone [phone number]. [Add restocking fee, if any.] [Add brands or products that cannot be returned, if any.]
The lesson's sample policy refunds the full product price minus the original shipping charges and tells customers to request this by email or phone.
The refund policy must state any restocking fee and any brands or product types that cannot be returned, because a reviewer checks for these.
The refund and return policy should answer: what the refund policy is, how a customer requests a refund, how returns work for damaged items, and how a customer starts a return.
Source B's example refunded the original shipping cost for store-caused returns and did not refund it for remorse returns.
The 2025 template in Dropship defaults: store refunds original shipping cost for defective or wrong items.
Default refund policy settings for a new dropship store: the customer pays for return shipping, the store pays for defective or wrong items and refunds the original shipping cost,
Refunds, timing, cancellations (continued)
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t:
orders canceled before shipping receive a full refund, and exchanges use prepaid shipping labels.
Cancellation policy: full refund if canceled before shipping.
Original shipping cost policy: the original shipping cost is refunded for store-caused returns.

For a steam shower or bathtub that fails local inspection, the return is the purchase price minus the original shipping fee, the return shipping fee and a 15% restocking fee if it is in original packaging.
If opened or assembled, the restocking fee rises to 25%.
Refund disputes are best prevented with clear product page wording about returns. Keep the wording specific to the supplier and product type. (2020)

A refund dispute can happen when a return promise is inconsistent (see Consistency).
Return address and RMA:
The RMA process: a customer starts a return and receives an RMA number. The return address is provided after the return is authorised.
Procedure: after you receive an RMA number, send the item only to the return address you are given, quoting the RMA number.
If returns go to a third-party warehouse instead of the business address, the refund policy must state that the return address is provided after the return is authorised.

Google may flag a policy that does not clearly name the return address when it differs from the business address.
Template for a warehouse return address:
Once your return has been approved and you have received an RMA number, we will provide you with the exact return address of the warehouse facility.
Please send your item only to that address, quoting your RMA number.

Include this summary table at the top of the refund policy page, titled "Returns and Refunds at a Glance":
**Restocking fee**: None (state explicitly if zero)

**Return window**: [your return window]
**Refund timing**: [your refund timeline, stated clearly]
**Return method**: RMA required

**Return address**: Provided after RMA authorization, may differ from business address
**Shipping costs**: [exact cost, or free shipping]
Damage reports and defective items
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: Set the two damage report windows separately in the returns policy, because the carriers' claim periods differ.
Damage reports for shipments by UPS or FedEx must be filed within 48 hours by the customer. For all other carriers the damage report window is 15 days.
Conflict on UPS and FedEx: the Example for high-ticket products sets freight (LTL) damage reports at 48 hours after delivery and small parcel shipments via UPS or FedEx at 15 days after delivery.
The Shopify default sets UPS or FedEx at 48 hours and all other carriers at 15 days. Check the carrier's claim period before you publish, because the two sources do not agree on UPS and FedEx.

Damage report window by carrier type (applies to the high-ticket template):
Freight (LTL): 48 hours after delivery.
Small parcel (UPS or FedEx): 15 days after delivery.
Each area of a competitor's return policy has its own terms: seller errors (wrong or damaged product, incorrect photo), the window for reporting damage, warranty terms, and change-of-mind returns.

Record each separately.
Restocking fees and damage: damage to the product can void the return entirely.
For a quality or damage claim, the customer provides photo or video evidence. State that a refund is not granted simply for disliking a product; the customer can leave a review instead.
The 30-day money-back guarantee applies, with photo or video evidence required for quality or damage claims.
Keep screenshots of the terms of service, shipping policy and refund policy pages. They serve as evidence in a chargeback dispute.
Put a specific refund cutoff in the refund policy, such as no refunds after 14 days from delivery, and state it in the terms of service as well.
Publish clear terms of service, a shipping policy and a refund policy with specific conditions, such as no refunds after a set number of days.
Exchanges
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: Exchanges are only offered for defective or damaged items. The customer must send details of the issue and proof of damage.
The customer pays return shipping, which is non-refundable in the sample policy.
Replacements happen only for defective or damaged products. The customer emails the contact address describing the problem and attaches proof of damage.
Exchange shipping: "Customer responsible for return and reshipment costs" is the example input.

Exchanges use prepaid shipping labels in the default settings for a new dropship store.
Template for returns and exchanges:
Returns and Exchanges We accept returns and exchanges within [X-day] days for unused products in their original packaging.
If you are not satisfied with your purchase, contact us at [email/contact info] to start a return.
We will guide you through the process and issue a refund or an exchange once we have received and checked the returned items.
Show each brand's warranty on its product pages in an expandable section that is unique to that brand. (2024)

Warranty blurb for product pages: "We offer a [warranty length] warranty on all [Brand] products. This warranty is limited to [scope, for example parts only] and covers [short description of what it includes].
Place it directly under the warranty statement on each product page of that brand.
We offer a [warranty length] warranty on all [Brand] products. This warranty is limited to [scope, for example parts only] and covers [short description of what it includes].
Warranty on a product's warranty tab: replace the manufacturer's email address with your own business email so customer questions reach your company.
The manufacturer still handles warranty claims, so redirect customers to them only when a claim is needed. (2026)
Source B's warranty example: 12 months on appliances and 3 months on spare parts from purchase.
Warranty text and guarantees (continued)
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: Items that are impractical to send back, such as an installed refrigerator, may have their warranty handled on site by an authorised service agent instead of a return.
Note this exception separately, since it changes the returns process for bulky or installed products.
The product guarantee page should explain how the guarantee works, when a product counts as not effective, and how long the guarantee lasts.
Because each supplier may have different terms, the page can list the guarantee for each supplier's products.
Using example return and warranty terms without changing them to match your own returns policy and each supplier's policy will cause problems.
Terms must be verified and adjusted before use.
Sources disagree on whether to match each supplier individually or use one blanket policy with exceptions.

Each applies in the case stated:
Match each supplier individually: "Don't create uniform policy; match supplier policies individually."
Use one blanket policy with exceptions only for suppliers that do not accept returns. (2021 onwards)
Use one general policy for most suppliers and give unique policies to suppliers whose terms differ. (2023)
Use one standard 30-day return policy for the store and add exceptions only for extreme outliers. This keeps the policy simple. (2023)
Use a blanket return policy built from the average of your suppliers' return policies.
Set your return and shipping policy as an average of the supplier policies. Do not copy each supplier's policy into the store.
For a store with several brands, use one general return policy that works for all suppliers, or add a separate return policy tab on each product page for a brand with different terms. (2023)

When each applies:
Use the blanket policy when most suppliers share similar terms, and show exceptions separately.
Blanket policy versus supplier exceptions (continued)
p.s: Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

p.t: Use an individual supplier policy when supplier terms differ widely, such as a supplier with no returns or a supplier with a 14-day window.
Supplier return terms differ in windows, restocking fees and return shipping. Because of this, a blanket policy can sometimes cost around $100 on a single return.
Main shipping and return policy covers most products. Any supplier with stricter terms gets its own policy on the product page, and those exclusions are also listed in the main policy.
If a supplier refuses returns for a product, mark the product as not eligible for returns on its page, or ship it to a fulfilment centre you control.
Write one general return policy that fits most suppliers. List the exceptions on the returns page with footnote markers, and repeat them on the product pages of the affected suppliers.

Build the return page this way (2023):
1. Put the general return policy at the top and add the note "some exclusions apply".
2. Below it, list each supplier or brand the general policy does not cover.
3. Under each listed supplier, state its specific return policy. Place a product-level return policy on the product pages of those unique suppliers.
Use one general return policy when most suppliers share similar terms, and give unique policies to suppliers whose terms differ.
If a supplier's agreement states that no products are returnable, you can still sell their products by setting a separate policy for that supplier that marks the products as non-returnable.

Expect higher return rates in some niches. (2023)
A store policy based on the supplier's policy: "Base your return policy on your suppliers' return policies." (2020)
Older advice (2019) return policy procedure for the returns page:
1. On each brand's product page, show that brand's return policy in the returns tab (for example, Company A policy equals 15 days).
2. On the returns page, state the general store return policy at the top.

Return policies must match across all pages. Inconsistent policies between the product page and the returns page confuse customers.
Keep a separate policy for each supplier when supplier terms differ. The supplier-specific wording goes on each supplier's product pages.
Principle: create one combined shipping and returns policy that covers most suppliers. Suppliers whose terms differ get their own policy text on the policy pages and in the product page tabs.
Products from non-returnable brands and suppliers are excluded from the general policy and stated separately (see Non-returnable items).

A customer-facing returns template that works for all suppliers: "If your item arrives damaged or defective, we will replace it or refund it, and we will cover the cost of shipping the replacement or the return.
If you want to return an item that is not damaged or defective, you may return it within 30 days of delivery; you are responsible for the return shipping cost, and a restocking fee may apply.
Items must be returned in their original condition. (2023)
If your item arrives damaged or defective, we will replace it or refund it, and we will cover the cost of shipping the replacement or the return.
If you want to return an item that is not damaged or defective, you may return it within 30 days of delivery; you are responsible for the return shipping cost, and a restocking fee may apply.
Items must be returned in their original condition.

Steps to create the shipping policy with an AI prompt (Settings > Policies > Shipping policy):

1. **Copy** the full shipping policy prompt, from its copywriter role line (the first line that tells the AI what job to do) to the end.
2. **Paste** it into ChatGPT or another AI tool.

3. **Enter** the store name.
4. **Enter** the support email in the format support@yourdomain.com.
5. **Set** the shipping region to Continental United States only, for a US business. (This means the 48 connected US states, not Alaska or Hawaii.)

6. **Keep** the default handling time of 3 to 5 business days, transit time of 3 to 7 business days and total delivery time of 7 to 12 business days. (Handling time is how long it takes to get an order ready to ship.
Transit time is how long it spends on the road. Business days are working days, not weekends.)
7. **Leave** the shipping partners at their default. (Shipping partners are the delivery companies.)
8. **Set** the freight option to yes for large and heavy products. (Freight means shipping by truck.)
9. **Delete** the white glove delivery field, unless it is confirmed available for your niche. (White glove delivery means the carrier brings the item inside and sets it up.
Your niche is the product group you sell.)
10. For out of stock or custom orders, **enter** that customers are contacted with updated timelines. (Out of stock means not on hand.)
11. For delays, **enter** that customers are proactively notified when delays occur. (Proactively means you tell them first, without waiting for them to ask.)

12. **Send** the prompt, copy the generated policy and paste it into the Shipping policy in Shopify.
13. **Click Publish.**

1. **Click** the Refund and return policy. It first shows as "no policy set."
2. **Copy** the full refund page prompt, from its copywriter role line to the end.

3. **Paste** it into ChatGPT or another AI tool.

The customer pays **return shipping**.

Exchanges use **prepaid shipping labels** (labels the store has already paid for).

Prompt for a plain-language returns and exchanges policy. Use it word for word. Fill in your own values before you send it.
Act as a senior eCommerce customer-experience writer. Draft a plain-language Returns & Exchanges Policy for a Shopify store that sells high-ticket goods sourced from domestic suppliers.

The copy should ease buyer worry, state expectations openly, read as an established and dependable business, stay simple to follow, avoid legal jargon, never use the word “dropshipping,” and feel fair
and centered on the customer. Voice: professional, reassuring, transparent, supportive, confident. Use short section headers and brief paragraphs. Length: 400 to 650 words.

p.t: Skip filler, exaggeration, and boilerplate. It should read like a genuine brand's own page.
Include these sections: Policy Overview; Return & Exchange Eligibility; Return Window; Return Shipping Responsibility; How to Start a Return or Exchange (RMA Process); Damaged or Defective Items;
Cancellations; Refund Processing Time; Our Error vs. Customer-Initiated Returns; Exchanges Process; Final Reassurance Statement.

and reshipment costs] Do You Use Prepaid Return Labels?

reduces hesitation on high-ticket purchases, makes the brand feel safe to buy from, can be pasted straight into Shopify, and is unique each time it is generated. Use no placeholders.

A high-ticket returns policy (high-ticket means expensive products) should state the refund time as a **fixed number of business days** after receipt and inspection (see Refunds).

Keep the copy between **400 and 650 words**, with short section headers.
High-ticket buyers hesitate most when they cannot see the cost and effort of a return.
The policy should answer three things: who pays return shipping, whether a restocking fee applies, and how the original shipping cost is treated.

Clear answers reduce worry about buying more than long reassurance text does.
